back: A past value of the series, y(t-k), made with shift(k). It is safe because it uses only data before the target.

front: What does a first difference remove? A seasonal difference?
back: First difference diff(1) removes a trend. Seasonal difference diff(m) removes a season of period m.
r = p(t) / p(t-1) - 1. Returns combine by multiplying (1 + r).

front: Log return formula and main advantage?
back: g = ln(p(t) / p(t-1)). Log returns add up over time, so the sum over a period equals ln(last / first).

front: How do you get a price back from log returns?
back: p(t) = p(0) * exp(cumulative sum of the log returns up to t).

front: Do +10% then -10% return to the start price?
back: No. 100 * 1.1 * 0.9 = 99. In log returns, ln(1.1) and ln(1/1.1) cancel exactly.
